newsitem.title: USA: Portland Genl says rate cut could cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: Portland Genl says rate cut could cut jobs.

text.p: The rate cut proposed by staff of the Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) "could force" Portland General Electric Co (PGE) to consider employee and service reductions, the utility said Monday.
As a condition of the planned merger of Portland General Corp (PGC), PGE's parent, with Enron Corp, the OPUC staff has said the utility's rates should be cut by $47.4 million annually for four years.
The two companies, however, estimate cost savings of about $3 million from the merger.
Ken Harrison, chief executive officer of PGC, said the staff's recommendation suggests that the OPUC should subsitute the merger approval process for a normal cost of service prodceeding.
"This position concerns me because it would send a message that someone asking for permission to merge with an Oregon company that owns a utility may get unfairly treated," he said.
PGC maintains that cost savings from the utility's non-regulated businesses, such as power trading, should not be passed on to customers since they do not assume the risks of those businesses.
The OPUC will hold a public meeting February 14 to continue the merger review.
